title: 1D Interface-Induced Real-Space Berry Curvature Gradient Encoded in SpinValley-Coupled Nonlinear Photocurrent in Lateral Heterostructure
authors: Suman Kumar Chakraborty, Jinu James, Biswajeet Nayak, David Tebbe, Purbasha Ray, Christoph Stampfer, Bernd Beschoten, Lutz Waldecker, Prasana Kumar Sahoo
abstract: Symmetry breaking enables helicity-dependent optoelectronic responses in quantum materials. In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), circular photocurrent (CPC) is typically observed under oblique illumination via the circular photon drag effect, while realization of the intrinsic circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE) under normal incidence remains challenging. Here, we report a clear signature of CPGE in chemical vapor deposition-grown monolayer 2D lateral heterostructure (LHS). By probing the nonlocal photocurrent across the 1D hetero-interface, we observe a helicity-dependent photocurrent consistent with a spin-valley-coupled CPGE-dominated mechanism driven by interface-induced Berry-curvature asymmetry, i.e., Berry curvature dipole. Spatially and spectrally resolved measurements under selective excitation of the MoSe2, WSe2, and the interface regions exhibit distinct magnitudes and polarities of the CPG responses. These contrasting behaviors highlight the opposite spin-valley dichroism for MoSe2 and WSe2, as well as enhanced valley mixing at the 1D interface. Our findings establish LHS as a robust platform for realizing a hetero-interface-induced CPGE-like response and highlight its potential for valleytronics and optospintronics.
summary: This work reports the observation of the intrinsic circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE) in a 2D lateral heterostructure (LHS) using nonlocal photocurrent measurements. The effect is attributed to a spin-valley-coupled mechanism driven by interface-induced Berry-curvature asymmetry. The findings establish LHS as a promising platform for advancing valleytronics and optospintronics.
main_problem: The realization of the intrinsic circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE) under normal incidence in 2D materials, which is challenging to observe.
main_result: The authors report a clear signature of CPGE in a 2D lateral heterostructure (LHS) by probing the nonlocal photocurrent across the 1D hetero-interface.
method: Nonlocal photocurrent measurements were performed across the 1D hetero-interface, with spatially and spectrally resolved measurements under selective excitation of constituent materials.
model_or_system: The system is a chemically vapor deposition-grown monolayer 2D lateral heterostructure (LHS) composed of TMDs like MoSe2 and WSe2. The physics is governed by spin-valley coupling and interface-induced Berry-curvature asymmetry.
key_observables: Helicity-dependent photocurrent (CPGE-dominated mechanism), Circular Photocurrent (CPC) responses, and the magnitude/polarity of the CPG responses.
important_parameters: 1D hetero-interface, MoSe2 and WSe2 excitation, normal incidence illumination.
main_assumptions: The observed photocurrent is dominated by a spin-valley-coupled CPGE mechanism driven by the interface-induced Berry-curvature dipole.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context by contrasting oblique illumination effects (CPC) with the difficulty of observing normal incidence effects (CPGE). It then presents the experimental observation of CPGE in LHS, followed by detailed analysis of spectral and spatial variations across the interface.
why_interesting: The study uses optoelectronic measurements in 2D materials to probe fundamental quantum phenomena like Berry curvature and spin-valley coupling, which are highly relevant to understanding topological and spin-orbit coupling effects in quantum systems.
